**Role type: Max term contract, full time (1 year, until January 2028\)**


**Role grade: Pharmacist (Unregistered)**


**Shift details: Monday to Friday plus ability to work weekends as per roster requirements**


**Department and location: Pharmacy, St Vincent’s Public Hospital, Sydney**


**Salary: $82,253\.78 \+ Super \+ Salary Packaging**

  



**Welcome to St Vincent’s Hospital Sydney**


Join a team built on a proud legacy of world\-class care, true compassion, and deep community roots.


Founded by the Sisters of Charity and powered today by St Vincent’s Health Australia, the Sisters' legacy of compassionate service is our living heartbeat. As Sydney’s premier and iconic inner\-city public hospital, we serve the entire population, providing world\-class care to all people, including the most vulnerable in our community. Across our renowned precinct, we feature cutting\-edge programs and surgery infrastructure, fostering clinical excellence and professional growth.


Located in the vibrant heart of Darlinghurst, we are positioned just minutes from Kings Cross station, with direct, high\-frequency bus connections from the east, and seamless links from Gadigal and Museum stations right to our doorstep.


Read on to explore this exciting role and the fantastic perks waiting for you here.


**About the role**


**Under the supervision of a Pharmacist:**


* Support the delivery of inpatient and outpatient pharmacy services, developing your clinical skills in medication management and pharmaceutical care planning
* Develop your skills in patient counselling, medication education and the provision of drug information to patients, carers and other healthcare professionals
* Gain hands\-on experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing, including the preparation of extemporaneous pharmaceuticals and applying relevant quality and safety controls
* Participate in pharmacy practice research, including undertaking a specific research project
* Work collaboratively within the pharmacy team, participate in weekend rosters and undertake other duties as required by the Director of Pharmacy or Deputy Director of Pharmacy

**About you**


* Successful completion of a Pharmacy Degree and eligible for provisional registration with AHPRA plus eligibility to enrol in an approved Intern Training Program prior to commencement **(You must upload a copy of your academic transcript as part of your application)**
* Sound knowledge of pharmacology and the ability to apply this knowledge in practical clinical situations
* Excellent written and oral communication skills, with demonstrated interpersonal skills and the ability to effectively counsel patients and carers and collaborate with healthcare professionals at all levels
* An understanding of the role of a Hospital Pharmacist, including professional, ethical and legal responsibilities, with a commitment to ongoing professional development, continuing education, quality improvement and research
* A proactive and adaptable team player with demonstrated initiative, strong problem\-solving, time management and prioritisation skills, and the ability to work independently, meet deadlines and contribute effectively within a busy team environment

**What we can offer you**


* **Exceptional Rewards:** Competitive pay and not\-for\-profit salary packaging to maximise your income
* **World\-Class:** Be part of a renowned precinct alongside the Garvan \& Victor Chang institutes
* **Excellence:** Premier heart/lung transplant program, advanced robotics, \& pioneering HIV/AIDS initiatives
* **Cutting\-Edge Oncology:** Deliver advanced cancer care and trials at the renowned Kinghorn Cancer Centre
* **Community:** Support vital programs for First Nations, homelessness, mental health, \& drug and alcohol care
* **Professional Advancement:** Accelerate your career with study leave and Curran Foundation scholarships
* **Health \& Wellbeing:** Fitness Passport, discounted private health, \& cultural recognitions and celebrations
* **Coming from NSW Health?:** Smooth transfer of your qualifying service and leave entitlements

**Sponsorship / work rights for** **Australia**


Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.


**Equal opportunity**


We celebrate diversity \& inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.


As part of our commitment to reconciliation, we encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples to apply and join us in delivering care that heals body, mind, spirit and community.


**How to apply**


The closing date for applications is **30th September 2026\.**


Shortlisting for this position will commence immediately. We encourage you to apply promptly as the advertisement may close early should a suitable applicant be sourced.


**Please ensure you upload a copy of your academic transcript as part of your application. Applications without an academic transcript will not be eligible for review.**


Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with each of the things listed in the About You section of this job advert.

  


Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

Optimize services and solutions for our global clients across all lines of business. Gain an unparalleled view of our leading financial organization while driving our clients' businesses forward with strategic support and end\-to\-end process management.




**What you Can Expect**




As a trainee in the 2027 Sydney Traineeship Program within JPMorgan Chase, you will participate in a 2\-year full\-time paid program, gaining essential knowledge and skills to build a dynamic, long\-term career with us. You will have the opportunity to work on either the Operations or Finance \& Business Management tracks, optimizing services for global clients or engaging in financial analysis and reporting. You will act as a trusted advisor, ensuring the integrity of financial statements, and contribute to strategic business decisions. You will also complete the nationally recognized qualification Financial Markets Certificate from the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA).




Operations


Optimize services and solutions for our global clients across all lines of business. Gain an unparalleled view of our leading financial organization while driving our clients' businesses forward with strategic support and end\-to\-end process management. We're looking for results\-oriented individuals with enthusiasm for developing strategies that optimize business operations.


Finance and Business Management


Finance \& Business Management offers challenging opportunities to work on local regulatory reporting, month end close process and project\-related work on new products/or system implementation. You will get to understand a wide range of different derivative products, the implications of control issues and their potential impact on the legal entity financial statements and regulatory filings. We are looking for highly motivated individuals who have a passion for analysis that will help drive strategic business decisions.


Team allocation will be based on business needs.

**Job responsibilities**

* Act as a trusted advisor to business and group heads by identifying, escalating, and mitigating business risks and optimizing business performance by driving key initiatives.
* Responsible for ensuring the overall integrity and validity of the financial statements and controls over the transaction cycle; performing critical reporting and controls functions for the organization.
* Create meaningful analysis and reporting in support of our businesses. Coordinate with partners across the firm to provide financial and strategic analysis, creation, oversight, and coordination of budgeting and forecasting.
* Contribute to programs that are large scale and comprised of multiple projects and work streams.
* Create effective procedures and support process improvement that are adhered to company standards.
* Ensure timely completion of team tasks and responsibilities.
* Become a key Intelligent Solutions member and work on automation initiatives across the team.
* Actively engage in learning the operational processes within Operations.
* Represent team through a wide array of People initiatives across the organization.




**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Must be a current Year 12 student and have obtained a high school certificate by the time the program commences
* Must not have commenced or graduated from a degree, Certificate IV qualification, or higher at the time the program commences. **Participation in the Traineeship Program requires full\-time commitment; simultaneous enrollment in other studies is not allowed.**
* Must be Australian citizen or Permanent Resident
* Strong attention to detail
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* Comfortable working in teams to deliver results
* Highly motivated with a ‘can\-do' attitude
* Ability to multi\-task and work in a fast\-paced environment
* Available to start work in March 2027




**Application Period:**


August \- November 2026

**Application Deadline:**


20 November 2026 at 12:00noon AEDT


We encourage early applications as screening will be conducted on a rolling basis.

**Program Period:**


March 2027 – March 2029

**What's next?**

* Submit a complete and thoughtful application, which includes your resume. Your application and resume is a way for us to initially get to know you. It's important to complete all relevant application questions, so we have as much information about you as possible. We will review your application to determine whether you meet the required qualifications.
* If you are advanced to the next step of the process, you'll receive an email invitation to complete a video interview within 48hrs, powered by HireVue. This is your opportunity to further bring your resume to life and showcase your experience for our recruiting team and hiring managers.
* HireVue is required, and your application will not be considered for further review until you have completed this step. We strongly encourage that you apply and complete these required elements as soon as possible, since applications will close once positions are filled.




**Note:** This is a paid, full\-time program. Successful applicants must commit full time, simultaneous enrollment in other studies is not allowed. Students planning to attend university may explore our internship opportunities, which are open to penultimate\-year university students, on our Careers website.


For enquiries, please email us at aus.grad@jpmorgan.com


**ABOUT US**
  

  

J.P. Morgan is a global leader in financial services, providing strategic advice and products to the world's most prominent corporations, governments, wealthy individuals and institutional investors. Our first\-class business in a first\-class way approach to serving clients drives everything we do. We strive to build trusted, long\-term partnerships to help our clients achieve their business objectives.  

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.  

  

  

**ABOUT THE TEAM**
  

  

Our professionals in our Corporate Functions cover a diverse range of areas from finance and risk to human resources and marketing. Our corporate teams are an essential part of our company, ensuring that we're setting our businesses, clients, customers and employees up for success.

HKA is one of the world’s leading independent provider of consulting, expert and advisory services working on complex disputes, investigations and commercial matters.


At HKA, our Sydney Forensic Accounting \& Commercial Damages (FACD) team works on complex matters for lawyers, regulators and businesses across Australia and Asia Pacific. Our work can involve determining the financial impact of a dispute, assessing lost profits or other damages, performing business valuations, investigating financial information, and preparing analysis that may ultimately be presented as expert evidence in court or other proceedings.


As part of the HKA team you can expect:

* The opportunity to join a supportive environment where you will receive mentoring from world renowned experts.
* A diverse and vibrant office environment in Sydney with colleagues spread across different technical disciplines.
* A company that cares about its people and is committed to making a difference.

**The Opportunity**


We are offering an 8\-week paid internship for penultimate\-year students within our Sydney Forensic Accounting \& Commercial Damages (FACD) team, commencing in December 2026 and concluding in early February 2027, with a break over Christmas and New Year for our office closure period.


This internship is ideal for those looking to learn about the dynamic field of forensic accounting. You will work alongside experienced forensic accountants and expert witnesses, and have the opportunity to contribute to real client matters.


Depending on the matters you are involved in, you may:

* Analyse financial records and large datasets to identify trends, anomalies and key issues.
* Research companies, industries and markets.
* Assist with financial and damages calculations.
* Build and develop financial models in Excel.
* Help assess and interpret complex financial information.
* Contribute to reports, presentations and other work prepared for clients and legal teams.


This internship is designed to give you a genuine insight into what it is like to work as a forensic accountant and to help you develop skills that extend beyond the classroom.

**Who You Are**


You are a naturally curious individual who enjoys solving problems, asking questions, and digging deeper to uncover the story behind the numbers. Whether you're already interested in Forensic Accounting or simply looking for something different from a traditional accounting career, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.


To be successful in this role, you'll:

* Be in your penultimate year of study (graduating in 2027\), studying any discipline, but primarily Commerce, Finance, Economics, Data Analytics, Law, Criminology, Science or other related degrees.
* Enjoy tackling complex problems and thinking critically.
* Be comfortable working with uncertainty and navigating unfamiliar challenges.
* Have strong analytical skills and exceptional attention to detail.
* Be a confident written and verbal communicator.
* Enjoy working as part of a close\-knit, collaborative team.
* Demonstrate integrity, professionalism, and a willingness to learn.

**What We Offer**


At HKA we recognise that our people are critical to our ongoing success. Our priority is to provide an inclusive and collaborative culture aimed at providing the best opportunities for our people to thrive and develop in their chosen career path.


Interns will be required to work from our Sydney office five days per week. This is designed to maximise your learning through hands\-on experience, providing direct access to mentors and opportunities to collaborate closely with colleagues.

**Closing Date: 9 October 2026**

**ED\&I at HKA**


HKA has a thriving ED\&I committee working hard to provide an inclusive and welcoming environment for a truly diverse set of employees. We are committed as a business on the continued improvement of our Equality, Diversity and Inclusion strategy, please visit our careers page for further information or feel free to ask our recruitment team for further information.


All HKA employment decisions shall be made without regard to age, disability, gender or gender reassignment, marriage, and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, and sexual orientation, or any other basis in compliance with local legislation.

If you would like more confirmation, please feel free to email us at enquiries@hka.com to check the authenticity of a job posting.

We are seeking a highly motivated Research Fellow to join an interdisciplinary research group at Macquarie University focused on green hydrogen, electrocatalysis and sunlight\-driven photoelectrochemical fuel production.  

  

The group has established an advanced research platform for electrochemical and photoelectrochemical energy conversion, including electrochemical workstations, a solar simulator, an Incident Photon\-to\-Current Efficiency (IPCE) measurement system and a customised roll\-to\-roll magnetron sputtering facility. Researchers also have access to advanced characterisation capabilities and external synchrotron and photovoltaic facilities through national and industry collaborators.  

  

Current research directions include AI\- and data\-driven discovery of multielement catalysts, amorphous catalyst structure–activity relationships, water and seawater electrolysis, and integrated solar\-to\-fuel systems.  

  

**The Role**  

Working closely with Dr Doudou Zhang, Professor Vladimir Strezov and a growing network of national, international and industry collaborators, the Research Fellow will develop next\-generation catalysts and integrated devices for renewable\-fuel production.  

  

This position is particularly suited to an emerging researcher seeking to build a strong independent research profile through high\-quality publications, new research concepts, competitive grant applications, HDR supervision, and industry and international collaboration.


Key responsibilities include:

* Design, synthesise and optimise electrocatalysts and photoelectrochemical materials for hydrogen and sustainable fuel production.
* Conduct electrochemical and photoelectrochemical measurements, including CV, LSV, EIS, stability testing, product analysis and solar\-to\-fuel/device performance evaluation.
* Fabricate and optimise catalyst electrodes and devices, with opportunities to use scalable roll\-to\-roll magnetron sputtering fabrication.
* Undertake advanced materials characterisation and collaborate with national and international partners on specialised in\-situ/operando and synchrotron characterisation.

**About the Role:**
-------------------

We believe the Sales Development Representative (SDR) role at CrowdStrike is one of the strongest platforms to build a career in cyber security sales.
  

  

If you love talking to people and understanding their perspective, are curious about the cyber industry, and take pride in smashing goals, this is the role for you.


You'll join a team that works together in the office, brings the best out of each other and has fun doing it. Success means making an impact while you're in this role, and building the skills to move into your next one.

**What You'll Do:**

**Start conversations.**

* Reach out to organisations that don't use CrowdStrike yet, and understand their business and security objectives. Understand what they are worried about, what they are trying to achieve and educate them on the value of partnering with CrowdStrike.
* Conduct multi\-channel outreach via phone, email, and LinkedIn, focusing primarily on outbound prospecting while also following up on inbound leads sourced from campaigns, content, and event engagement.
* Ask relevant questions to determine whether there's a real problem CrowdStrike can solve, then book a meeting between the prospect and an account executive.

**Use AI well.**

* Research accounts thoroughly before you call, so you can form a perspective on the likely challenges a business is facing.
* Use AI to help you prioritise where your time goes, and to write outreach that's specific to the person you're contacting rather than generic.
* Go back through your own call recordings and transcripts, spot what's working and what isn't, and fix it.
* Try new approaches, track the results, and tell the team what you learned. Good ideas from this team end up in the playbook.

**Build real knowledge.**

* Learn the threat landscape and the CrowdStrike platform to communicate with enough depth and conviction to educate an industry security professional, but also simply and succinctly to a friend.
* Learn the cybersecurity market; the partners, vendors \& problems we jointly solve for customers.
* Learn how to take something complicated and explain it simply, so your conversations stay focused on the customer's problem rather than on product detail.

**Own your number.**

* You'll have a monthly target for qualified meetings booked, and uncapped commission for hitting and beating it.
* Know your own conversion rates at each stage. Understand how your daily activity turns into weekly and monthly results.
* Keep Salesforce up to date and your notes useful. It's how your account executive walks into a meeting prepared instead of cold.

**Work with your team.**

* Treat the relationship with your account executives as a partnership. You plan account outreach together and you share the outcome.
* Leverage marketing campaigns, assets and events and collaborate with our channel partners.
* Elevate each other's skills through roleplay, peer\-to\-peer feedback and best practice sharing.
* Work with the team in person \- we work 3 days a week in office.

**Grow into your next role.**

* You'll receive a comprehensive onboarding and solid grounding in professional selling, including frameworks you'll use for the rest of your career.
* There are proven progression certifications and trainings you'll work through during your time in Sales Development. They're designed to help ensure you are ready for account executive, account management, sales engineering or other roles.

**What You'll Need:**

* A real interest in learning, both the sales craft and the cyber security industry and a positive attitude towards feedback.
* Curiosity about AI and how to use it in your own work. You don't need to be an expert, but you do need to be willing to try things.
* Technical aptitude, and the ability to pick up new business and technical concepts quickly.
* Drive to hit your number and beat it, on your own and as part of a team.
* Clear communication, written and spoken. Listen, ask questions, and be clear about next steps.
* The ability to handle pushback. An objection usually means there's more to understand, not that the conversation is over.
* A genuine interest in building a career here.
* The ability to learn how to effectively use tools such as Gong, Salesforce, Sales Navigator and AI tools to ensure efficiency in the role.

**How We Show Up:**

We believe in what we sell. Nobody expects you to know everything on day one, but we do expect you to build real belief in what we're here to do, which is to stop breaches. When a customer raises a concern, we don't pretend it isn't there. We deal with it honestly. If you don't believe in what you're selling, your customer won't either.


We also care about how we treat people. We show respect to everyone regardless of their title, we lead with curiosity, and we know when to be serious and when not to be. The aim is that people come away from talking to you feeling better about themselves and about the company. Your teammates should see you as someone whom they can go to equally in victory and when they need advice or support.


If that's how you want to work, get in touch!

**Employment Type:** Permanent Full Time
  

**Position Classification:** Registered Nurse
  

**Remuneration:** $81,748\.16 \- $114,771\.98 per annum
  

**Hours Per Week:** 38
  

**Location:** Blacktown  

**Where you'll be working**
  

Join the Forensic Mental Health Services team at Budyari Gumada, Blacktown Hospital, supporting people with complex mental health needs in a contemporary clinical environment. Blacktown Hospital serves a rapidly growing and culturally diverse community and offers modern facilities designed to support exceptional care and staff wellbeing.
* Work in a modern teaching hospital with state\-of\-the\-art facilities and a strong focus on patient outcomes
* Enjoy dedicated outdoor staff areas and landscaped gardens designed to support wellbeing
* Be part of a teaching environment that provides opportunities to support university students and future health professionals
* Benefit from convenient access to Westpoint shopping centre, just a 10\-minute walk away
* Access onsite parking for a small fee, all\-day street parking and nearby Blacktown train station
  

**What you'll be doing**
  

As a Registered Nurse, you will provide high\-quality clinical care that promotes psychological and physical wellbeing, emotional health and recovery. Working closely with clients, families and the multidisciplinary team, you will contribute to safe, coordinated and person\-centred care.
* Deliver comprehensive, evidence\-based mental health assessment, care planning, treatment and evaluation
* Build therapeutic relationships and monitor changes in mental health to support timely clinical review
* Collaborate with multidisciplinary professionals to coordinate care and achieve individual health goals
* Maintain accurate clinical documentation while meeting professional, legal and organisational requirements
* Promote health, wellbeing and self\-management while contributing to quality improvement and contemporary clinical practice

**Ready to make a meaningful difference?**
Join NSW Health and grow your career in a supportive environment where your contribution matters.  

**How to Apply**
  

Apply online by submitting your resume and addressing the criteria listed below by providing examples that demonstrate your ability before the closing date.  

**Essential Requirements:**
Registration: Current Registration as a Registered Nurse with Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)  

**Selection Criteria:**
* Registered Nurse who has completed a new graduate RN program or experience working as a Registered Nurse
* Demonstrated experience working with people presenting with an acute mental health problem
* Demonstrated advanced reasoning skills with proven ability to work autonomously and as part of a multidisciplinary team within minimal direct clinical supervision
* Proven effective high level written and verbal communication skills, interpersonal skills and ability to exercise independent professional judgement when solving problems
* Working knowledge of the NSW Mental Health Act 2007
* Demonstrated ability to collaborate with consumers and carers regarding mental health care
* An understanding of the recovery philosophy and trauma informed care in Mental Health and the ability to implement these within clinical practice
* Current NSW drivers licence

working with us will ensure your professional life is provided every opportunity to succeed and develop in your chosen career role.

  

**About Us**


Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District (NBMLHD) is an exceptional environment to advance your career while enhancing your skills and expertise. As a recognised leader in the healthcare industry, we deliver a comprehensive range of public health services across the Nepean, Blue Mountains, and Lithgow Regions.

  

The Primary Care and Community Health Unit consists of 9 centres that provide a range of services for children, young people and their families, adults, older people and their carers. Our services range from health promotion, prevention and early detection through to assessment, treatment and continuing care. Our staff work in partnership with schools, GPs, hospitals, non\-government agencies and other organisations to provide care across our centres, in people’s homes, other community venues as well as virtual care (telehealth).
  

  

Are you a Registered Nurse who is passionate about supporting children and families during the early years of life? We are seeking dedicated Registered Nurses to join the Child and Family Health Nursing (CFHN) Service. This is a rewarding opportunity to work within a supportive multidisciplinary team, delivering evidence\-based care that helps children and families thrive.
  

  

CFHN Service forms an integral part of primary health care. The Registered Nurse Child and Family Health aims to improve and promote the optimal health, growth and wellbeing of children aged 0\-5 years and their families by providing safe, compassionate care through the assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation of nursing care in collaboration with families and the multidisciplinary team to achieve outcomes that meet the goals of the child and their family.
  

  

Working as part of the multidisciplinary team and utilising a strengths\-based family partnership approach, in line with the principles of Primary Health Care, the Registered Nurse will work in collaboration with clients, families and carers who attend the Child and Family Health Nursing Service to provide compassionate, evidence\-based, quality client\-centred nursing care to achieve identified goals and outcomes. This comprehensive service involves assessment, prevention, early identification and intervention, referral, health promotion, community development and education to clients of the service.
  

  

To be successful in this role, you will have a passion for family\-centred care, strong communication and relationship\-building skills, and a commitment to improving health outcomes for children and families. If you are looking for a flexible opportunity to contribute to a highly valued community service while continuing to develop your skills and experience, we'd love to hear from you.
  

  

**Benefits available to eligible NBMLHD employees**


* Opportunity for extra tax savings through Salary Packaging
* Novated Leasing
* Great education opportunities through Education Training Service which offers over 110 courses each year
* Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for staff and family members
* Fitness Passport

NBMLHD is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment which reflects the community we serve. We encourage candidates from all backgrounds, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, LGBTIQA\+, Cultural and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) people, neurodiverse individuals, and people with disabilities to apply.

  

NBMLHD is committed to implementing the child safe standards.

  

For assistance with applying through the NSW Health Career Portal please  

  



**What you will bring to the role**


* Current registration as a Registered Nurse (Division 1\) with the Australian Health Practitioners Regulation Authority (AHPRA)


* Demonstrated recent experience and clinical skill in provision of care to children aged 0\-5 years and their families/carers as a registered nurse (including completion of a new graduate RN program or 12 months full time equivalent experience working as a Registered Nurse)


* Demonstrated capacity to provide effective nursing care that is person centred, family inclusive and culturally sensitive to people accessing health services.


* Demonstrated ability to organise and prioritise work.


* Demonstrated effective communications written and verbal skills.


* Demonstrated commitment to professional development.


* Ability to work effectively within a multi\-disciplinary team.


* Current driver's licence and willingness to use for work purposes. This may include driving long distances across the LHD.
